releases.body:
Adds Doubao Search as the twenty-first search provider, using the Custom version of Volcengine's search API.

- Connect through `/connect` or set `OSP_DOUBAO_API_KEY`; select provider `osp-doubao`.
- Request up to 50 results, with optional source-authority and freshness filters.
- Choose full page content or query-relevant snippets. Content is capped at 2,000 code points per result by default; set `DOUBAO_CONTENT_CHARS=0` to keep all content.
- Parse both ISO and Beijing-time publication dates, and report API business errors even when returned with HTTP 200.
- Update English and Chinese documentation, package exports, and provider tests. Isolate the no-credential aggregate test from locally configured API keys.

Validation: README audit, TypeScript check, and all 27 test files passed (374 tests passed, 2 skipped); npm package dry run includes the new provider.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/guotree/opencode-search-plugin/compare/v4.2.1...v4.3.0

## What''s Changed

- **Registration is now fault-isolated.** A provider that fails while registering is reported on stderr while the other nineteen still load, so a bug in one plugin file costs one provider instead of the whole package. Interruption still propagates, so teardown is never mistaken for a failure.
- **SerpApi and Serper drop a malformed hit instead of failing the whole search.** Every organic result field is now optional -- as both files' comments always claimed -- items without a link are dropped the way querit and linkup do, and a schema-level decode failure carries the same friendly `Invalid ... response` prefix as a JSON-parse failure.
- **Closed-set env knobs report an unknown value instead of silently falling back,** matching the warn-and-drop Kagi and StepFun already document: `YOUCOM_EXTRACTION`, `LINKUP_DEPTH`, `ANYSEARCH_FORMAT` and `ANYSEARCH_ZONE`. `ANYSEARCH_ZONE` previously forwarded whatever it was given, so a typo failed every search.
- **Provider-specific tests for the eight providers that until now rode only the shared contract** (AnySearch, DeepSeek, Linkup, Metaso, Querit, SerpApi, Serper, You.com), plus `scripts/audit-readme.mjs`, which cross-checks both READMEs against the code.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/guotree/opencode-search-plugin/compare/v4.2.0...v4.2.1

## What's changed

### Fixed

- **The shared cache is now least-recently-used** (all nineteen providers). A cache hit used to return early without touching the entry's position, and a rewrite kept its old slot, so eviction always spent the oldest-inserted query regardless of how often it was reused — any working set larger than the 200-entry limit lost its hot queries in first-seen order. A hit now moves the entry to the tail and a rewrite counts as a use too, while the expiry timestamp stays anchored to the fetch, so a hot entry can outlive its neighbours but never its own freshness bound.

- **An empty result set is remembered for at most 30 seconds** instead of the full `<PROVIDER>_CACHE_TTL`. An HTTP 200 with zero results is truthy and was cached like any other answer, so a single transient upstream wobble — a reindexing window, a cold replica — locked retries out for ten minutes. Empty sets now pin for `min(CACHE_TTL, EMPTY_RESULT_TTL)`, with `EMPTY_RESULT_TTL` at 30 seconds; a non-empty answer still earns the full TTL it was billed for.

### Added

- **`test/cache.test.ts`** pins the three cache branches that previously had no test at all: eviction (a hot query survives insertion pressure, and the least recently used one is still spent once the limit is passed), expiry (including `CACHE_TTL=0`, and the TTL staying anchored to the fetch even when the entry is hit mid-life), and the empty-result pin.

- **The `Effect.forkScoped` rebind subscription is now asserted byte-for-byte** in the seventeen files that carry it — the sixth shared block and the only one without a guard — with the two keyless providers (anysearch, keenable) asserted to carry no subscription at all. `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s shared-blocks table lists it.

## Upgrade notes

Nothing to change. No provider ID, knob, endpoint or key variable was touched, and the cache is internal to each provider file: an existing configuration behaves exactly as it did on 4.1.0.

Two behaviours you may notice. A repeated query in a busy cache now survives eviction, so fewer searches are paid for twice. And a query that came back with no results is retried for real after 30 seconds instead of being answered "nothing" for ten minutes — for providers that bill every dispatch, retrying an empty query within that window is a billed round trip again, deliberately, in exchange for recovering from a transient wobble on its own.

## Install

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-search-plugin@4.1.1
```

## What's changed

### Added

- **StepFun** (`plugins/stepfun-search.ts`, `osp-stepfun`, `OSP_STEPFUN_API_KEY`) — the nineteenth provider, on StepFun's (阶跃星辰) standalone web search API at `POST api.stepfun.com/v1/search`. A bare retrieval endpoint — `query`, `n` and an optional `category` in, `results[]` of `{url, position, title, time, snippet, content}` out — with no model call in the loop. Billing is ¥0.04 per search.

  The endpoint takes three parameters and nothing else, so no paging, time range, domain filter or safe-search switch is exposed: `n` caps at 20, and the four documented scenario values (`programming`, `research`, `gov`, `business`) are the only lever. An unrecognised `STEPFUN_CATEGORY` is warned about and dropped rather than sent to earn a 400.

  Every hit carries `content` — the full page body — with no parameter to turn it off, so the snippet is read by default and `STEPFUN_INCLUDE_CONTENT` opts into the body, cut to `STEPFUN_CONTENT_CHARS` (4000) code points so no emoji is ever sliced in half. `time` is the page's index time and is reported as `published`, the only time field there is.

  The cn platform serves the only search endpoint (`api.stepfun.ai/v1/search` answers 404 while its chat endpoint does not), so there is no international twin to bind as a second provider. StepFun publishes no "empty searches are free" rule, so every dispatch is assumed billed and repeat queries ride the shared cache. Knobs: `STEPFUN_COUNT` (1–20, default 10), `STEPFUN_CATEGORY`, `STEPFUN_INCLUDE_CONTENT`, `STEPFUN_CONTENT_CHARS`.

The provider count is now nineteen. StepFun binds only while a key exists, so it is safe to sit in OpenCode's `random` pool.

### Changed

- **Adding a provider is now documented as a minor bump.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` gained a versioning table: a new provider, knob, endpoint or mapping field is minor; a major is reserved for a change an existing configuration cannot survive — a renamed provider or plugin ID, a renamed key variable, a provider split into two, or a provider removed. This release is the first to follow it.

## Upgrade notes

Nothing to change. `osp-stepfun` is new and registers only once `OSP_STEPFUN_API_KEY` or a `/connect` credential exists, so an existing configuration behaves exactly as it did on 4.0.0 — including a `random` pool that never picks it.

To use it, get a key from [platform.stepfun.com](https://platform.stepfun.com/interface-key), then either export `OSP_STEPFUN_API_KEY` or connect **StepFun Search (osp)** in `/connect`.

## Install

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-search-plugin@4.1.0

## What's changed

### Added

- **Z.ai** (`plugins/zai-search.ts`, `osp-zai`, `OSP_ZAI_API_KEY`) — the sixteenth provider, on Zhipu's international site Web Search API at `POST api.z.ai/api/paas/v4/web_search`. Same request and hit shape as the cn site, minus the two fields the intl spec does not define, with `search-prime` as the only engine. Billing is $0.01 per successful search with no free tier; repeat queries ride the shared cache. Knobs: `ZAI_COUNT` (1–50), `ZAI_RECENCY`.
- **Moonshot** (`plugins/moonshot-search.ts`, `osp-moonshot`, `OSP_MOONSHOT_API_KEY`) — the seventeenth provider, on Moonshot AI's (Kimi) international site Basic search API at `POST api.moonshot.ai/v1/tools/search`. A bare search endpoint — `text_query` plus `limit` in, `search_results[]` of snippets out — with no model call in the loop. Billing is $0.002 per search and only when the response carries at least one result (failed and empty searches are free). Knobs: `MOONSHOT_COUNT` (1–20, default 5), `MOONSHOT_INCLUDE_CONTENT` (opt-in full-page text per hit).
- **Moonshot CN** (`plugins/moonshot-cn-search.ts`, `osp-moonshot-cn`, `OSP_MOONSHOT_CN_API_KEY`) — the eighteenth provider, the China-site twin at `POST api.moonshot.cn/v1/tools/search`. Same request, mapping and filter story as the international site, in renminbi (¥0.01 per successful search). Knobs: `MOONSHOT_CN_COUNT`, `MOONSHOT_CN_INCLUDE_CONTENT`.

The provider count is now eighteen. All three new providers bind only while a key exists, so they are safe to sit in OpenCode's `random` pool.

### Changed (breaking)

The cn and intl sites of Zhipu's Web Search API are now two providers. `osp-zhipu` is the cn site only (`open.bigmodel.cn`, keys from bigmodel.cn); the intl site (`api.z.ai`, keys from z.ai) is the new `osp-zai`. The two are separate account systems — a key from one answers HTTP 401 against the other, and the engines and prices differ — so each now binds on its own credential instead of a `ZHIPU_SITE` knob aiming one provider's key at either host. `ZHIPU_SITE` is no longer read.

## Upgrade notes

If you set `ZHIPU_SITE=intl`, move to `osp-zai` with `OSP_ZAI_API_KEY` and the `ZAI_*` knobs. Credentials stored in `/connect` for `osp-zhipu` are unaffected and keep working. Both 401 messages now name the other site's provider, so a key on the wrong endpoint points at its fix.

## Install

```sh
opencode plugin add opencode-search-plugin@4.0.0
```
